facts.anchor: But Sunday morning, as I tried to sketch rain gliding down the conservatory’s glass walls, Gazzie cracked open the door and asked me to meet her on the front porch.

facts.fact: Virginia 抢救了蔫掉的植物
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia had rescued her wilting plants while we were at work
her voice vibrated with energy
A lizard scurried toward the porch then, an inch away, abruptly changed direction and retreated into the grass

facts.fact: 动物不碰 Greer House 的口径
facts.anchor: I still hadn’t seen an animal touch Greer House besides Gazzie’s pet hatchling, but it was caged, and somehow that didn’t count.
the stray gray cat huddled beneath the bushes, out of the rain
an entire foot of it was crispy, burned, like someone had sprayed acid in a neat perimeter
There’s the matter of Ida.

facts.fact: 谈话岔开对 Michelle 的思绪
facts.anchor: this conversation was already taking my mind off Michelle
that Greer House has a certain—presence
The bathwater reflection, the muttering voice, the shadowy figure flitting in and out of rooms.
I’ve noticed…something.
So, she still guides our family, keeps us on the right track.
She manipulates the house. Everything from the walls to the air.
I remembered Leon’s door slamming. How, when I’d opened it again, the air was dense, frigid. Unwelcoming.

facts.fact: 关／毁／挪的清单＋磷酸盐名片
facts.anchor: She put the phosphate people’s business card on my desk after I dismissed the idea.

facts.fact: 日记进水槽的真凶改判
facts.anchor: maybe she hadn’t been the one who’d snuck into my room and thrown Uncle Leon’s journal in the sink. Ida had.
I’ll make her let me go or die trying.

facts.fact: 「我以为他指的是 Gazzie，难道是 Ida？」
facts.anchor: I thought he’d meant Gazzie. Had he been referring to Ida?

facts.fact: 全信 haint 的时点自供
facts.anchor: This was the moment I started to believe in Ida Greer’s haint wholeheartedly.
I was glad we sat on the porch, where she probably couldn’t reach us.
So you’re already acquainted.

facts.fact: Ida 要家族做什么：扩张清单
facts.anchor: Keep expanding across Florida with our farms, the phosphate pit, the sugarcane investments

facts.fact: 农场四项问题全归 Ironheart
facts.anchor: The problems at the farm—the leaks, the algae, the mold, the kudzu—they’re all Ironheart.
I still hadn’t experienced anything definitive on the farm that made me take stock in the mythical ghost alligator.

facts.fact: Ida 让它保持距离的机制
facts.anchor: She makes it keep its distance—as long as we’re doing our part.

facts.fact: 边界伸缩理论＋近来两件事
facts.anchor: I’d caught Nova and agreed to join the running for heir.
Keep her spirit alive. Feed her.
I had a terrible image of a skeleton sitting, Psycho-style, in the attic, mouth open, waiting for a spoonful of grits
She’s in the portraits. That’s how she’s anchored here.

facts.fact: 从垃圾桶那张复制品起就知道不对
facts.anchor: I’d known they were off since the moment I pulled that copy out of the trash.

facts.fact: 通灵会起源（少女时问病）
facts.anchor: As a girl, she’d contacted her ancestors through a séance for answers to her illness.
preferably one that held some of their remains, like a pendant containing a lock of hair

facts.fact: 画师把头发放进每幅像
facts.anchor: She had her painter place strands of her hair in each portrait

facts.fact: 维多利亚传统与 Mama 的略过
facts.anchor: Now I knew why Mama had skimmed over that era.
It’s why I restore them myself. Can’t trust any old artist with precious materials like that.
“Grow up,” Gazzie snapped

facts.fact: 指甲盖涂云的恶意想象
facts.anchor: Were there fingernail clippings glued onto the painted clouds?
We don’t have enough originals to hang up at the farm—hence the problems there—but we do have the one, so there’s enough of her to keep Ironheart at bay.
So does restoring the paintings…feed her?
About once a month, I also make an offering.
I sacrifice a gator.
Don’t you—we—kill thousands every year?
I raise a few gators especially for the purpose. Give them special attention. Keep them in their own pen.
“The hatchling on your desk,” I breathed.
When they’re large enough, I call to Ida and finish it.
Slit their throats.
Such a slow death.
“Can’t we just use a gun?” I asked. “Do it fast?”

facts.fact: 「要象征性的，她喜欢逗留此刻」
facts.anchor: It has to be symbolic,” she said plainly. “That’s what she likes. To linger in the moment.
Like the moment I stood over Michelle, relishing the way her eyes widened in fear.
We’d moved from family myth into family cult territory. I’d dismissed Nova’s accusation, but now—
made an executive decision—or, perhaps, received permission—and stood
I followed her to a half-height door sealed with a rusty latch. A crawl space.

facts.fact: 爬行空间反而干燥凉爽
facts.anchor: the crawl space was surprisingly dry and several degrees cooler than outside
Twenty feet ahead lay a pile of white sticks
Alligator bones.
Hundreds of them.
Tiny claws and long spines. One that resembled a human’s arm bone. Complete skeletons. Skulls.

facts.fact: 骨堆中心在房子正下方
facts.anchor: The bone pile’s center must have been located somewhere under the middle of the house.

facts.fact: 熟悉的嗡声从地板渗下
facts.anchor: A familiar, high-pitched hum seeped through the house’s flooring above me
It was the soft, feminine voice I’d heard in Greer House’s hallway. This time, it spoke directly into my left ear.
Ida was down there with me.

facts.fact: 空气变稀＋被反锁的恐惧想象
facts.anchor: I imagined the door slamming shut, trapping me in the crawl space with the voice and the bones
“Aren’t they beautiful?” she asked, almost moaning with pleasure.
But Gazzie was right behind me, her eyes glinting in my phone’s light.

facts.fact: Ida 埋骨的公开说辞与真话
facts.anchor: She told people it was a reminder of how we made our money. But she told me the truth.

facts.fact: 「她要 Ironheart 记得她赢过他」
facts.anchor: She wanted Ironheart to remember she’d bested him.

facts.fact: 以她之名杀的都迁来此处
facts.anchor: Each animal we kill in her name is stripped and relocated here.
Caroline used to call Greer House ‘The House Built on Alligator Bones.’ Clever, no?

facts.fact: Mama 的短语：既是比喻也是字面
facts.anchor: The Greers built their fortune on alligator bones. Mama’s phrase was metaphorical and literal.
A single claw bone spilled from its opening. “A little initiation.”

facts.fact: 剥皮本是正经活＋拯救论
facts.anchor: I reminded myself that farms like ours had saved alligators from extinction.
I still remember the feel of those bones—smooth and cold as judgment.
Harrison must have been excused from initiation rites; he wasn’t family.
“Can’t we just visit Ida’s grave or something?” I asked feebly.

facts.fact: 「Ida 在这儿，不在土里烂」＋口令
facts.anchor: Ida’s here, not rotting away in the earth. Now,” she continued confidently, “repeat after me. Ironheart’s death was our beginning.

facts.fact: Mama 在衣橱里改写短语
facts.anchor: Mama had changed the phrase in her closet, transforming it from an invocation into a condemnation.
I had the terrible feeling that by speaking them aloud, I was indicating that I accepted my family’s haint
“Ironheart’s death,” I said quietly, “was our beginning.”
the buzzing ratcheted up. It hummed louder and louder, my breath quickening alongside it
Pushing past Gazzie, I scrambled out from under Greer House.

facts.fact: 焦界扩到十英尺＋蜥蜴干尸
facts.anchor: ten feet of brown grass where living blades had been only minutes before
“What happens if we don’t?” I whispered.
“She gets what she wants, one way or another.” Facing the house, eyes unfocused, she looked haunted. I sensed she was fighting off tears.

facts.fact: Mama 离岛原因的扩容猜想
facts.anchor: Maybe Uncle Leon’s tragic death wasn’t the only thing that drove Mama from Amelia Island.
Maybe Ida Greer had something to do with it, too.
